attempts.plan:
1. Read the borough-level table that contains  
   • borough name  
   • recorded-crime per 10 000 residents for 2H-2011  
   • recorded-crime per 1H-2012.  
   Also read the list of neighbor pairs (undirected).

2. Handle the two variables’ single missing values as follows:  
   • For any borough that is missing EITHER the 2H-2011 or the 1H-2012 value, drop that borough entirely.  
   • After dropping, update the neighbor list so that any references to the removed borough disappear.  
   • The remaining N boroughs (N ≤ 33) will have no missing data.

3. Compute the change variable:  
   Δ_i = (1H-2012)_i – (2H-2011)_i for each remaining borough i.

4. Mean-center the change variable:  
   z_i = Δ_i – mean(Δ).  
   (No need to divide by the standard deviation because Moran’s I formula only requires centered values; the denominator uses Σ z_i².)

5. Build the spatial weights matrix W:  
   • W_ij = 1 if boroughs i and j are neighbors, 0 otherwise, with zeros on the diagonal.  
   • Row-standardize W (divide each non-zero row by its row sum) so S0 = Σ_i Σ_j W_ij = N.

6. Calculate Global Moran’s I on the centered change values:  
   I_obs = (N / S0) * (Σ_i Σ_j W_ij z_i z_j) / (Σ_i z_i²).  
   Because W is row-standardized, the N/S0 factor simplifies to 1, but keep it explicit in case some rows become isolated after dropping a borough.

7. Permutation (randomization) significance test:  
   • Shuffle the z values randomly across the N boroughs 999 times (≥ 500 as required).  
   • For each permutation p, compute I_p using the same formula.  
   • Two-sided p-value = (number of permutations where |I_p| ≥ |I_obs| + 1) / (999 + 1).

8. Decision rule:  
   • If p < 0.05 and I_obs > 0 → conclude that changes cluster spatially (neighboring boroughs tend to show similar direction/magnitude changes).  
   • If p < 0.05 and I_obs < 0 → significant spatial dispersion (neighbors tend to change in opposite directions).  
   • Otherwise → no spatial pattern in the change variable.

9. Report the observed Moran’s I and p-value and state either “CLUSTERED” or “NOT CLUSTERED” according to the decision rule.

10. End the answer with exactly one line in the required format, inserting the computed statistic and p-value.

(This plan uses only pandas and numpy, drops any boroughs with missing data, and applies a 999-permutation Global Moran’s I test to determine whether the change in recorded crime per 10 000 residents clusters spatially across London boroughs.)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------ 1. Load the data ------------------
crime_path = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_second_half_2011_to_first_half_2012.csv'
adj_path   = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

crime = pd.read_csv(crime_path)
adj   = pd.read_csv(adj_path)

# ------------------ 2. Drop boroughs with any missing values ------------------
crime = crime.dropna(subset=['second_half_2011_value', 'first_half_2012_value']).copy()

# ------------------ 3. Compute the change variable ------------------
crime['change'] = crime['first_half_2012_value'] - crime['second_half_2011_value']

# ------------------ 4. Prepare adjacency (keep only remaining boroughs) ------------------
valid = set(crime['borough'])
adj = adj[adj['borough'].isin(valid) & adj['neighbor'].isin(valid)]

# ------------------ 5. Build a row-standardised spatial weights matrix ------------------
index = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(crime['borough'])}
N = len(crime)

W = np.zeros((N, N))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i, j = index[row['borough']], index[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = W[j, i] = 1            # undirected graph → symmetric

row_sums = W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
row_sums[row_sums == 0] = 1          # avoid division by zero for any isolated rows
W = W / row_sums                     # row-standardised
S0 = W.sum()                         # ΣΣ w_ij

# ------------------ 6. Global Moran’s I ------------------
z   = crime['change'].values
z   = z - z.mean()

I_obs = (N / S0) * (z @ W @ z) / (z @ z)

# ------------------ 7. Permutation test (999 random shuffles) ------------------
np.random.seed(0)
n_perm  = 999
I_perm  = np.empty(n_perm)

for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm    = np.random.permutation(z)
    I_perm[p] = (N / S0) * (z_perm @ W @ z_perm) / (z_perm @ z_perm)

p_val = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------ 8. Verdict ------------------
verdict = "CLUSTERED" if (p_val < 0.05 and I_obs > 0) else "NOT CLUSTERED"

# ------------------ 9. Required prints ------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {N}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (test statistic = {I_obs}, p = {p_val})")
